facts: Displacement is a vector, while the distance between the two positions is its magnitude, a single number.
$\underset{\sim}{r}(t_{2})-\underset{\sim}{r}(t_{1})$ subtracts the earlier position from the later one, in that order.
Reversing the order reverses the vector, so the two answers differ only by a minus sign.
For a displacement $a\underset{\sim}{i}+b\underset{\sim}{j}$, the distance between the positions is $\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}}$.
The displacement is the straight-line change in position, not the distance travelled along a curved path.
A zero displacement means the particle has returned to where it started.

The direction is the angle measured anticlockwise from the positive $x$-axis. For a displacement $a\underset{\sim}{i}+b\underset{\sim}{j}$ with both components non-zero, find the reference angle $\alpha=\tan^{-1}\left|\dfrac{b}{a}\right|$. Use the signs of $a$ and $b$ to select the quadrant: the direction is $\alpha$, $180^{\circ}-\alpha$, $180^{\circ}+\alpha$ or $360^{\circ}-\alpha$ in the first, second, third or fourth quadrant respectively. Along the positive $x$-, positive $y$-, negative $x$- and negative $y$-axes, the directions are $0^{\circ}$, $90^{\circ}$, $180^{\circ}$ and $270^{\circ}$ respectively. Zero displacement has no direction.
steps: Find the position vector at each of the two times.
Subtract the earlier position vector from the later one.
If a distance or a direction is asked for, find the magnitude or the angle of that displacement.

workedExamples.question_text: A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=(t^{2}+2)\underset{\sim}{i}+(3t-5)\underset{\sim}{j}$. Find its displacement from $t=1$ to $t=4$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
$\begin{aligned}\underset{\sim}{r}(1)&=3\underset{\sim}{i}-2\underset{\sim}{j}\\\underset{\sim}{r}(4)&=18\underset{\sim}{i}+7\underset{\sim}{j}\end{aligned}$

Subtract the earlier position from the later position.

$\begin{aligned}\underset{\sim}{r}(4)-\underset{\sim}{r}(1)&=(18-3)\underset{\sim}{i}+(7-(-2))\underset{\sim}{j}\\&=15\underset{\sim}{i}+9\underset{\sim}{j}\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text: A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=8\cos t\,\underset{\sim}{i}+8\sin t\,\underset{\sim}{j}$. Find its displacement from $t=\dfrac{\pi}{6}$ to $t=\pi$, and the exact distance between these positions.

A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=3t\underset{\sim}{i}+(12-t^{2})\underset{\sim}{j}$. Find its displacement from $t=2$ to $t=5$ and its direction, measured anticlockwise from the positive $x$-axis to the nearest degree.

A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=t^{2}\underset{\sim}{i}+5t\underset{\sim}{j}$ for $t\ge0$. Its displacement from $t=1$ to a later time $T$ is $35\underset{\sim}{i}+25\underset{\sim}{j}$. Find $T$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
$\begin{aligned}\underset{\sim}{r}(1)&=\underset{\sim}{i}+5\underset{\sim}{j}\\\underset{\sim}{r}(T)&=\underset{\sim}{r}(1)+35\underset{\sim}{i}+25\underset{\sim}{j}\\&=36\underset{\sim}{i}+30\underset{\sim}{j}\end{aligned}$

Compare the horizontal components.

$\begin{aligned}T^{2}&=36\\T&=6\end{aligned}$

Since $T>1$, the negative root is excluded. The vertical component agrees: $5(6)=30$.

workedExamples.question_text: A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=t^{2}\underset{\sim}{i}+3t\underset{\sim}{j}$ for $t\ge0$. Its displacement from $t=a$ to $t=a+3$ is $33\underset{\sim}{i}+9\underset{\sim}{j}$. Find the two times.
workedExamples.solution_text:
$\begin{aligned}\underset{\sim}{r}(a+3)-\underset{\sim}{r}(a)&=\big((a+3)^{2}-a^{2}\big)\underset{\sim}{i}+\big(3(a+3)-3a\big)\underset{\sim}{j}\\&=(6a+9)\underset{\sim}{i}+9\underset{\sim}{j}\end{aligned}$

Compare the horizontal components.

$\begin{aligned}6a+9&=33\\6a&=24\\a&=4\end{aligned}$

The vertical component is already $9$, as required. The two times are $t=4$ and $t=7$.
